title: Health ministry proposes curbs on prescription drug ads by retailers, wholesalers and distributors
summary: The union health ministry has proposed extending advertising restrictions on prescription drugs to retailers and distributors. This change will bar them from advertising certain medicines without prior government approval. The amendment affects drugs covered...

contentHtml:
New Delhi: The union health ministry has proposed to extend restrictions on advertising prescription drugs to retailers, wholesalers and distributors, barring them from advertising medicines covered under Schedules H, H1 and X without prior approval from the central government.

The requirement is already in place for pharmaceutical manufacturers under the existing regulatory framework.

Schedules H, H1 and X cover prescription medicines, including certain antibiotics and psychotropic drugs that require medical supervision.

Also read: Pharmacies, drug distributors may need approval to advertise prescription medicines

The proposed amendment to the Drugs Rules, 1945, seeks to extend the same requirement to entities licensed to sell or distribute these medicines by inserting a new sub-rule (22) under Rule 65.

The ministry has notified the proposal following recommendations of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB).
